title: arxiv_2501.03674v2
universal_lens: The hierarchical pose-guided multi-stage contrastive regression unifies spatio-temporal visual and skeletal manifolds via a physics-structural prior. By mapping dynamic sub-actions to variable-duration topological segments, the operator minimizes temporal discontinuity errors, establishing an isomorphic bridge between biomechanical kinematics and continuous state-space evaluation.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the multi-scale visual-skeleton encoder into a Bayesian posterior over latent biomechanical states. Conformal inference bounds are applied to the segmented sub-action features, ensuring rigorous uncertainty quantification for fine-grained athletic variances. The contrastive regression yields calibrated probabilistic quality scores with strict coverage guarantees.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the procedure segmentation network as a non-Markovian state-transition engine. Physics structural priors from skeletal graphs dictate valid situational transitions between diving phases. The multi-modal fusion module continuously updates the situational reasoning tensor, dynamically adapting to variable-duration sub-actions without fixed-frame discretization artifacts.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by recognizing the fundamental flaw in fixed-frame discretization (Quote 3): it introduces artificial boundary conditions that violate the continuous nature of biomechanical dynamics. To resolve this, we construct a hierarchical skeletal encoder (Quote 5) that projects high-dimensional video data $I \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}$ onto a sparse graph manifold $\mathcal{G}(V, E)$, where nodes represent joints and edges represent bone constraints. This projection acts as a dimensionality reduction operator that filters out background noise, isolating the intrinsic degrees of freedom of the athlete. 

Next, the dynamic procedure segmentation network operates on this manifold. Instead of slicing time uniformly, it identifies critical points where the derivative of the skeletal configuration exceeds a threshold, effectively partitioning the timeline into variable-duration sub-actions $\{\tau_k\}$. This ensures temporal continuity is preserved within each segment. These segmented features are then fed into a multi-modal fusion module, utilizing physics structural priors (Quote 8). Here, the skeletal graph provides a rigid constraint matrix, while dynamic visual features supply texture and velocity cues. 

Finally, the multi-stage contrastive regression (Quote 9) formulates the quality assessment as a metric learning problem. By pulling embeddings of high-scoring dives closer to an ideal prototype and pushing low-scoring ones away, the model learns a discriminative latent space. The dualities lie in balancing static posture correctness (e.g., entry angle) with dynamic fluidity (e.g., rotation speed). Failure modes emerge when the skeletal tracker loses precision during extreme motion blur, collapsing the graph manifold and rendering the subsequent segmentation and regression mathematically ill-posed.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits from classical biomechanics, specifically inverse kinematics and Euler-angle parameterization of human motion. It modernizes these concepts through deep graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and contrastive self-supervised learning. Historically, sports evaluation relied on discrete event detection; this primitive retroactively generalizes those heuristics into a continuous, differentiable optimization landscape, bridging symbolic rule-based judging with end-to-end neural perception. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two opposing agents: the Athlete (optimizer) seeking to maximize aesthetic and technical scores by exploring the boundary of physical limits, and the Judge (evaluator) attempting to map complex, high-speed trajectories onto a bounded scalar score. The AQA system acts as a surrogate judge, internalizing the cognitive biases and hierarchical attention mechanisms of human experts. It must anticipate the athlete's intent (e.g., attempting a higher difficulty dive) and adjust the baseline expectation accordingly, effectively playing a game of strategic inference against the athlete's performance distribution.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity and leakage, we enforce strict orthogonality between the visual appearance branch and the skeletal structural branch. If the visual encoder begins to rely heavily on background cues (e.g., pool tiles or lighting) rather than pose geometry, the physics structural prior acts as a veto, penalizing predictions that deviate from biomechanically plausible joint configurations. Furthermore, the multi-stage contrastive loss includes a regularization term that vetoes overfitting to specific athletes, ensuring the learned metric generalizes across diverse body morphologies and movement styles.
